comments.author: @kathyb-007
comments.text:
- Driving across the island in just two hours is actually impossible. The distance between the two furthest points, Negril and Morant Point, is about 180 miles. When you factor in the narrow roads, heavy traffic, and congested towns, the trip would take at least five to six hours.
- Roads shutting down for land crabs crossing? Lol. Wrong island. You must be thinking of Christmas Island, an Australian territory. If crabs cross roads in Jamaica, people just maneuver around them, or hit the roadsides with buckets to catch them for crab soup!
- SNOW? In Jamaica? For real? Well ok, the Blue Mountains do get cold and experience heavy frost at the peaks, but there is no research or official records I can find of actual snow falling on the island.
- "Nobody really speaks English there" and visitors will "understand nothing"??? Good Lord. Kingston is the largest English-speaking city in the Caribbean for a reason. In fact, Jamaica itself is the largest English-speaking country south of the United States in the entire Western Hemisphere by population! The whole island speaks English. You might not understand them when they start twanging the Patois but trust me when I say, everyone can not only understand English perfectly well but also speak it to visitors. The question is, do they want to? English is their native, official language. Choosing to speak Patois is purely a cultural preference, not a lack of fluency.
- Two oceans!!?? Last time I checked, Jamaica was surrounded by the Caribbean Sea, unlike Cuba and the Dominican Republic.

A FEW BONUS FACTS:
- Despite what people think, Jamaica has become a major regional leader in infrastructure, world-class fiber-optic Wi-Fi, and cable networks. Now, you might not know it the second you step off the plane because some of the local community roads are still really bad with potholes, but the massive new highway systems are top-tier and are continuing to develop more and more each day. Their fiber-optic internet setups are so advanced that the speeds easily blast past what millions of homes in America are still stuck with, especially since large parts of the US are still struggling on outdated, slow copper lines!
- Expanding more on their great water filtration system, because of natural limestone filtering, Jamaica is also one of the very few tropical islands in the entire world where locals and tourists can safely drink the tap water straight from the faucet! In fact, it is a known maritime fact that massive international cruise ships deliberately pull into the ports (Ocho Rios anyone? Hello!), just to buy it and completely fill up their drinking water tanks before heading back out to sea. This top-tier water system isn't even new—Jamaica was way ahead of the game! Falmouth actually had a running municipal piped water system all the way back in 1799. That means Jamaica had clean water pumped straight into homes long before major cities across the Americas did!

I could go on and on... but i won't. 😊

I am 80 years old
I went to Knox College where we wore sweaters it was so cold. We had students who were from Europe then and they wore their sweaters and warm jackets. I remember hearing then of something that reminded of a mixture of ice and snow. The bauxite industry in those days has Europeans and very few Jamaicans. The father of my best friend worked in the bauxite area and she and her sister attended school in Jamaica for that reason. They had friends at Munro College who were also from Europe. I visited the bauxite area with them to visit their father and I was the only black one there. By the way my poor Aunt who lived nearby discovered that she had ore that they were mining. They convinced her to surrender the property with the ore because she was doing it for her country. She did not receive one penny. She gave up the land with great pride since she was convinced that she was helping her country!
